author: Brenton Kemp
title: Jose Trevino record three-hit effort in loss to Orioles Saturday
desc: Reds catcher Jose Trevino went 3-for-4 with a double, a run scored, and an RBI in an 8-5 loss to the Orioles on Saturday.
impact: The veteran backstop kept cooking on Saturday, recording his second three-hit effort in as many days, including a three-run homer on Friday. On Saturday, he doubled in a run and scored on a TJ Friedl triple in the second inning, singled in the third, and singled in the sixth. He is slashing .267/.279/.367 with a homer, seven runs, and eight RBI through 63 plate appearances on the season.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Joey Gerber optioned to Triple-A
desc: The Mets optioned Joey Gerber to Triple-A Syracuse.
impact: Gerber will return to Triple-A to make room for Guillo Zuniga.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Guillo Zuniga called up by Mets
desc: The Mets called up reliever Guillermo Zuñiga.
impact: Zuñiga last pitched in the majors in 2024. He'll figure to be in a low-leverage role.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Patrick Sandoval (biceps) makes final rehab start Saturday
desc: Patrick Sandoval threw 68 pitches in his final rehab start on Saturday.
impact: Sandoval allowed one hit and one walk while striking out seven over five scoreless innings for Double-A Portland. He is hopeful to be activated later this upcoming week.

author: Nate Miller
title: Jose Ramirez (hand) has begun to swing
desc: Jose Ramirez (hand) has been hitting off a tee recently.
impact: Ramirez has already begun to swing a bat, and he is expected to take part in batting practice soon. Originally given a timetable of 6-7 weeks to return from a fractured hamate bone, Ramirez remains on track to return in late July or early August.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Shane Bieber roughed up in loss to Mariners Saturday
desc: Blue Jays right-hander Shane Bieber allowed seven earned runs across four innings while taking the loss on Saturday against the Mariners.
impact: Bieber pitched a scoreless first inning, but the Mariners got to him for five second-inning runs on the back of a Randy Arozarena grand slam. He allowed a two-run homer off the bat of Dominic Canzone in the fifth inning before recording an out and was pulled from the game after 89 pitches, 53 of which were strikes. The veteran has largely struggled in his return from the injured list, posting a 9.00 ERA across three starts and just 13 innings, going 0-1 in the process. He will look to shake off some more rust in a road matchup with the Padres on Friday.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Munetaka Murakami (hamstring) to run bases Sunday
desc: Munetaka Murakami is scheduled to run the bases on Sunday.
impact: If all goes well, Murakami will go on a rehab assignment on Monday. He could be activated from the injured list later in the week.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Robert Hassell III designated for assignment
desc: The Nationals designated Robert Hassell III for assignment.
impact: Hassell loses his spot on the 40-man roster for Washington. He will head to waivers as a result.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Eddy Yean has contract selected by Nationals
desc: The Nationals selected the contract of Eddy Yean.
impact: Yean will add a fresh arm for Washington in Sunday's series finale.

author: Nate Miller
title: Jean Cabrera designated for assignment
desc: Jean Cabrera was designated for assignment by the Phillies on Sunday.
impact: Cabrera was removed from the Phillies' 40-man roster to make room for Bryan De La Cruz to be added. Cabrera has struggled at both the Double-A and Triple-A levels this season, posting a 9.10 ERA over 15 starts.

author: Nate Miller
title: Bryan De La Cruz signs MLB deal with Phillies
desc: Bryan De La Cruz signed a Major League deal with the Phillies on Sunday.
impact: De La Cruz had been in the Phillies' organization on a minor-league contract all season before opting out recently. The 29-year-old outfielder re-signed with the club Sunday morning and was added to the 40-man roster. De La Cruz will be sent back to Triple-A for the time being. Jean Cabrera was designated for assignment in a corresponding move.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Keider Montero earns three-inning save Saturday against Rangers
desc: Tigers right-hander Keider Montero pitched three shutout innings while earning the save against the Rangers on Saturday.
impact: A seventh-inning walk to Evan Carter was Montero's lone blemish on the afternoon, as he was otherwise excellent despite not recording a strikeout of any of the 10 batters he faced. The right-hander was recently moved to the bullpen with a sudden logjam of healthy starters in the rotation, but Montero appears to be a young arm on the rise. The 25-year-old now owns a 3.21 ERA across 18 outings (15 starts), but his underwhelming 16.2% K% has him sitting with a 4.81 xFIP and a 4.70 SIERA, suggesting some regression could be heading his way.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Jack Flaherty sharp again in win over Rangers Saturday
desc: Tigers right-hander Jack Flaherty pitched 5 2/3 scoreless innings while earning the win in a 3-0 victory over the Rangers on Saturday.
impact: Flaherty was just about as good as it gets in this one, allowing just three hits without walking a batter while punching out five Rangers hitters on the afternoon. He came just one out shy of a quality start, but has pitched 10 2/3 scoreless innings while allowing just five hits and three walks while striking out 14 in two starts since returning from the injured list. He owns a 4.60 ERA in 17 starts this season, but hasn't allowed more than three earned runs in a start since May 17. He lines up to take on the Phillies at home on Friday.

author: Nate Miller
title: Salvador Perez (elbow) back in the Royals lineup
desc: Salvador Perez (elbow) will return to the Royals starting lineup Sunday.
impact: Perez has not played since Wednesday due to a sore elbow, but the veteran slugger will be back in action Sunday. Perez will bat sixth in the DH spot.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Riley Greene homers to power Tigers past Rangers Saturday
desc: Tigers outfielder Riley Greene went 2-for-4 with a two-run homer in a 3-0 win over the Rangers on Saturday.
impact: Greene's first-inning two-run homer proved to be more than enough for the Tigers in a 3-0 win on Saturday afternoon. The long ball was Greene's 12th of the season and took place on the same day he was named to the American League All-Star team for the second consecutive season. The 25-year-old is slashing .287/.375/.455 with 12 homers, 45 runs, 40 RBI, two stolen bases, and an .830 OPS across 88 games so far this season.
